column8: Wed 18 Nov: store for 3d; CASE's two counts (committed when promised, received when paid) are a recipient's counts, so Laura's figure enters the residency's or facility campaign's total, never a co-sponsor's own campaign; beside Q18-005 and Q18-006.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; the card itself says the FAQ line is about donor control after receipt, and row 3 shows CASE's conditional test is an expectation, so never call it a control test; and her Treasuries stay hers (held for her) until paid, so never say her promise moves them out of her control (funder test).

Wed 18 Nov: 3c or 3d reserve, the new part is the clash (CASE counts a conditional pledge on an expectation, FASB says probability is not a factor), so pledged is not booked; fix the use cell: a co-sponsor's conditional pledge sits in the residency's campaign total, not its own; rules alone are Q11b-032 and Q18-002.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d reserve, the plainest one-line proof that a campaign total and a ledger differ; Stevens quote re-read at source tonight word for word; pairs with row 3 and Q90-029; for judges only, never in Laura's words.
Wed 18 Nov: Houston applies CASE's reasonable-expectation rule already held in Q11b-032; the five-year window adds nothing a part needs.
Wed 18 Nov: one dollar amount and a payment schedule is UVM's rule in Q67-043 (and Q18-011); Fresno's president review of large conditional pledges is store detail.

Wed 18 Nov: store for 3d, the pledge card's own words (no contingencies or conditions) are what round 8's Mine comes first and carries no condition says in plain English; confirms a settled line, so F 2; beside Q67-043.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d store contrast, a known figure that can be withdrawn counts as $1; drop not withdrawn from the use cell: whether her 2031 statement can be taken back is Q77's question (a legal one outside the case), so say only that hers is owned and stated in writing.
Wed 18 Nov: employer matching gifts, not challenge pledges; anticipated matches not counted is already Q67-044 (and Q18-007); SKELETON 3d never offers a match on her figure.
Wed 18 Nov: Kent State restates CASE's reasonable-expectation rule held in Q11b-032; twin of row 5.
Wed 18 Nov: a specific dollar amount and schedule is UVM's wording in Q67-043; Caltech's line that counting differs from the books is row 4's point.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d store, a vivid practitioner line (an unnamed sum is recorded as $0), quotes re-read at the forum tonight; drop the funder-test link: framing A told readers to count the bottom and framing B was also stated as a range, so the test does not show a range read at its bottom; a forum post, never a standard.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; a matching claim is a notation, not money, the recipient's record of a co-sponsor's conditional pledge; Q18-007 holds the counting rule.

Wed 18 Nov: store; EWU counts an uncertain bequest at the donor's stated minimum, so never generalise to the lower of two numbers is the one written down; a bequest of unknown size, not an owned figure; beside Q71-021.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d reason for leading with one figure, but drop the funder-test explanation (framing A told readers to count the bottom; both framings stated $95,000 to $115,000); the sources speak of unknown or uncertain sums, not an owned range, and say nothing of ranges in those words; near Q18-011 and Q71-021.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; Ask, Expected and Funded are the recipient's CRM fields, so it is the residency's gift officer, never a co-sponsor's, who types her figure in; trivia for 3d.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c store, fundraisers forecast as amount times likelihood, so an owned figure sits at full value; drop discounted twice (the source's low-high field serves annual-report bands, not the forecast) and make it the recipient's forecast, not a funder's.
Wed 18 Nov: the same amount-times-probability field in Salesforce; twin of row 17.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; a campaign display that shows a match as not counted yet; 3d is Laura's words, not a campaign thermometer, and one help page is thin.

Wed 18 Nov: store for 3d and 3e, the giver's side: a co-sponsor pledging on the December 2032 condition books nothing until the total is promised; US-GAAP givers only; adds the giver's side to Q90-029.
Wed 18 Nov: giver and receiver booking on the same day is row 20 plus Q90-029's residency side.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; superseded US text (pre-2018), history beside Q18-002's removed remote-chance rule.

Wed 18 Nov: store for 3d, FASB's disclosure group raising matching gifts by a specified date is the co-sponsors' December 2032 condition in accounting words; read in a codification copy, so S 4; beside Q90-028.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d guard with its reason: the December 2032 sentence names the co-sponsors' pledges, since an unscoped condition is presumed to cover every figure (Q18-003's rule); SKELETON and round 8 already say so; say could be read as conditional, not would book as nothing, since the residency may not use US GAAP.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d store, its best use is the rename: CASE's own ANZ standard changed new funds secured to new funds committed (Feb 2026), the word the four funders used and the reason the report never says secured; documented, not oral; quotes re-read at source tonight.
Wed 18 Nov: store-only context; a Taiwanese regulation for health foundations (Taiwan law is outside the case's scope); same rule as FASB's giver side, row 20.
Wed 18 Nov: store-only context (Taiwan regulation, health sector); its use, a broker statement proves ownership and not the promise, is already Q99-001's comfort-letter point.
Wed 18 Nov: store-only context; Taiwan's culture-foundation standard defers to EAS; the auditor's habit decides is Keel inference; Taiwan law, outside the case.
Wed 18 Nov: store-only context; a draft framework in a commissioned study, not law; a promise alone creates no present obligation.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d store, a Taipei arts body books a gift as income when cash arrives, so her 2031 figure is counted and relied on, not booked, until paid in 2033; audited practice, not law; one foundation.

Wed 18 Nov: store; one grant-maker's own books (board-approved grants as payables, cancelled grants back as income), never in Taiwan a co-sponsor's board approval is when its promise becomes debt; Table 3 watches the plan and her figure is unconditional, so a board-date row needs a plan response first; figures not re-read tonight (balance sheet not in the text layer).
Wed 18 Nov: 3d store beside H7-070 and the fading-pledge reserve: a company's promised sponsorship to Taiwan's national arts foundation slipped a year (2022 accounts); one line in one year.
Wed 18 Nov: store-only context; one medical foundation's own manual keeps the remote-chance test FASB deleted; not a standard.

Wed 18 Nov: store; IPSAS 23 is a recipient's revenue rule, so a public co-sponsor that gives never books her pledge either way; say it as: public recipients book pledges only as cash; IAS 37 is Q106-016.
Wed 18 Nov: store for 3d or 3c context: outside US GAAP an individual's pledge usually reaches the books when paid (UK SORP), so FASB's receivable on promise is the exception; with rows 30 and 34.
Wed 18 Nov: Hong Kong's research-matching scheme counts gifts only when ownership moves, the strict-funder point in Q18-009 (matchable only in 2033); Q75 holds the arts match.
Wed 18 Nov: tandem anchoring is H7-065; this card read only the abstract and summaries, and a negotiation offer is not a gift range, so the toward-$95,000 use is unverified.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d confirms SKELETON's one figure, but not every book: CASE counts and US-GAAP recipients carry it, while IPSAS, the UK SORP and Taiwan's EAS practice book it only when paid (rows 30, 34, 35); say $115,000 on today's figures; commitment words are Q18-004.

Wed 18 Nov: restates SKELETON 3d's settled rule (the bottom said once as the part held since January 2028); drop the funder-test reading: framing A was told to count the bottom, so the test shows funders count what she tells them, not a range's bottom by default.

Wed 18 Nov: store; a co-sponsor's conditional pledge counts in the residency's campaign, not its own; the December 2032 date belongs to 3d's words, and a Table 3 row fits only if the plan acts on it, since her $115,000 is unconditional.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; 3d keeps her figure first and unconditional with no clause added; a give-back clause is a legal drafting choice resting on Q77's Taiwan law, outside the case; never suggest wording her pledge this way in the report.
